title: Bounded arithmetic: truth tests and proof construction

based_on.title: An Introduction to Gödel's Theorems, second edition, corrected Logic Matters reprint

summary: Build numerical and bounded-formula proof certificates with explicit internal loop invariants.
abstract: A statement whose quantifiers have numerical bounds can be tested by a finite calculation. Can Peano arithmetic also prove that this calculation produces a valid proof? For each fixed bounded formula, we construct two procedures: one builds a proof when the formula is true, and the other builds a proof of its negation when it is false. Bounded universal statements require assembling proofs of all their instances; a failed universal statement instead supplies a counterexample. Induction verifies that the resulting proof records pass the actual checker. This turns finite truth tests into proof constructions whose correctness the system itself establishes.
